Hong Kong Automotive Workers’ 2021 Walkout Caused Significant Disruptions, Industry Recalls

HONG KONG, 10 June – Industry figures and union representatives are reflecting on the unprecedented walkout staged by automotive sector workers in Hong Kong in May 2021, which led to a week-long shutdown of key assembly and repair facilities and affected companies including SJM Holdings Co Ltd.

The work stoppage, which began on May 17, 2021, saw more than 1,200 mechanics, assembly line operators, and logistics staff from major automotive firms in Kowloon and the New Territories halt operations. The industrial action, organized by the Hong Kong Automotive Workers’ Union, was called over pay disputes and concerns about workplace safety protocols during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Production lines across several facilities, including SJM Holdings Co Ltd and the local manufacturer Harbour Motors, were forced to close or operate at reduced capacity. The walkout delayed deliveries of new vehicles and disrupted the supply of spare parts to dealerships in the region, leading to a backlog of customer orders and extended wait times for repairs.

Industry analysts estimated that the week-long action resulted in a production loss of nearly 800 vehicles and spare part shortages that persisted for several weeks after operations resumed. “The walkout exposed vulnerabilities in the sector’s supply chain and highlighted the importance of dialogue between management and workers,” said Raymond Chu, an analyst at the Hong Kong Institute of Automotive Technology.

SJM Holdings Co Ltd confirmed at the time that its main service center in Kwun Tong suspended operations for five days, leading to a reported backlog of 300 vehicles awaiting repair. “The event was a wake-up call for all stakeholders,” said Pauline Wong, spokesperson for the company. “We have since taken significant steps to improve communication and address employee concerns.”

Union leaders said the strike yielded an agreement on hazard pay and strengthened safety measures. “It was a difficult decision, but necessary for our members’ well-being,” said Lee Ka-ho, vice-chairman of the Automotive Workers’ Union.

The automotive industry in Hong Kong has since returned to normal operations, and no disruptions are currently reported. However, sector representatives say the 2021 walkout remains a defining moment in recent industry history.
